niche_preference_profile: Prefers interfaces that feel structured, polished, and intentionally composed: clear stacked sections, strong hierarchy, visible content without extra interaction, restrained but premium styling, centered or balanced headers, muted or controlled color use in many product/settings flows, and minimal decorative noise. They also repeatedly like richer, more complete screens over sparse ones, and often favor calm system-like organization with cohesive cards, rows, and spacing. In some contexts they also respond positively to dramatic dark, high-contrast, premium-tech treatments, especially when paired with strong focus and clear action emphasis.

criteria.description: Prefers content broken into clearly separated stacked sections, cards, or labeled groups rather than mixed, blended, or undifferentiated layouts.
Prefers centered or balanced header composition with restrained top-bar framing over oversized, split, or top-heavy title treatments.
Prefers minimal ornamentation with fewer photos, carousel controls, floating imagery, and other promotional or distracting decorative elements.
Prefers strict alignment, consistent row structure, steady vertical rhythm, and orderly spacing that makes the interface feel rigorous and composed.
Prefers a practical, serious, system-like, utility-focused aesthetic over friendlier, promotional, tutorial-like, or generic consumer-app styling.
Prefers muted neutrals, dark navy emphasis, and soft pastel accents over brighter, louder, or more saturated accent palettes in standard product/settings flows.
Prefers repeated, consistent component patterns—such as unified cards, rows, icons, and control styles—over heterogeneous modules or mixed interaction treatments.
Prefers controls and actions that are explicit, well-defined, and visually decisive, with clear selectors, visible per-item actions, and strong CTA clarity rather than weak or ambiguous controls.
